objective: Deterministic prefix-only early abstention when observed evidence suggests continuing is not worth additional sampling cost, versus wait-until240 baseline.
method: Train 810 synthetic traces with frozen loss model; at checkpoints 140,180,220 evaluate frozen trailing100 HAC3 classifier. Candidate is early abstain ONLY when current label unresolved and feature-group empirical mean cost gain lower heuristic bound mean-1.64*SD/sqrt(n)>0 and group n>=25. Final240 decision unchanged if no authorized early action. Two authorized groups both at n220: unresolved, |slope/se|<2, low SE<.002. No early directional commits.

pilot.note: Inspected pilot then freeze committed; no post-freeze retuning.

prefix_suffix_mutation_audit.scenarios: Two deterministic future ramps ±8, for n=140,180,220; verifies prefix classifier only.

interpretation: SG057 is better than waiting under the stated synthetic loss model: reduce 12 false directional commits and 4420 observations at cost of withholding 26 correct decisions, leading to loss 31326→29944.8. Unlike SG054 and SG055 it stops early by abstaining, not by committing. Evaluation does not establish external robustness or globally optimal stopping.
limitations: Training uncertainty bound is heuristic and feature groups learned from synthetic training only, not coverage-guaranteed or robust to novel regimes.
The SG057 policy still abstains on 606/1080 streams; it is conservative rather than an always-correct classifier.
The measured lower loss relies on chosen penalties; result may reverse with higher abstention cost.
Known synthetic generator families with fresh holdout seeds, not real-world deployment.
Repo source uses sibling SG055 and SG052; re-fetch verification does not substitute for clean-checkout execution.
next: SG058 Unseen disturbance stress: test the frozen early-abstain policy on genuinely new generator mechanisms and compare whether its cost gain survives distribution change.
